name: Furen's Instructions
summary: In Stormwind, Furen's Instructions name the materials needed for fire-hardened mail. Furen Longbeard gives the parchment to Alliance warriors he has tested.

sections.title: A Master Smith's Demands
sections.body: Furen Longbeard offers to forge a resilient suit of mail for a warrior who has proved himself through simpler smithing work. The dwarven armorer asks the warrior to fetch the rare components himself. His parchment records what is needed and sends the warrior across continents to gather it.

sections.title: Exotic Components
sections.body: The parchment calls for a dangerous journey through the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. The hardened links need dozens of scorched spider fangs from damp caves in the Wetlands, along with horns from fire-breathing chimaeras in the crags of Stonetalon Mountains. The list also calls for a galvanized horn from the chimaera matriarch and a vial of volatile phlogiston held deep within Razorfen Kraul, a quilboar bastion.

faq.answer: Furen's Instructions are a written list Furen Longbeard gives Alliance warriors in Stormwind. It names the exotic materials needed to craft fire-hardened mail.
Furen Longbeard is a master dwarven armorer in Stormwind's Dwarven District. He tests seasoned warriors and makes durable protective gear for them.

faq.q: Where do the materials on the list come from?
aliases: where do i find the items
faq.answer: The list calls for scorched spider fangs from the Wetlands, charred horns and a galvanized horn from chimaeras in Stonetalon Mountains, and a vial of phlogiston from Roogug in Razorfen Kraul.

faq.q: What does Furen forge with these materials?
faq.answer: Furen uses the materials and his smithing secrets to forge a specialized piece of fire-hardened mail for the warrior.

angles.text: As an Alliance warrior, you face trials against fierce beasts and quilboar to earn heavy mail armor.
As a blacksmith, you can see how Furen's recipe combines beast reagents with rare alchemical distillations to temper armor beyond ordinary forging.
